# @nivinjoseph/n-eda

> TypeScript framework for event-driven architecture on Node.js: a partitioned, ordered, at-least-once event log backed by Redis, with dependency-injected event handlers, consumer groups, a distributed observer pattern, out-of-process consumers (AWS Lambda / HTTP RPC / gRPC), and built-in OpenTelemetry tracing. ESM only, Node >= 24.10, standard (ES2023+) TypeScript decorators. Redis is required — there is no in-memory implementation.

Install: `npm install @nivinjoseph/n-eda`

Sibling packages you will touch: `@nivinjoseph/n-util` (`Serializable`, `@serialize`, `Deserializer` — the event wire format; also `Duration` for topic TTLs and `DisposableWrapper`), `@nivinjoseph/n-ject` (the DI container — `EdaManager` wraps one; `ComponentInstaller`, `Registry`, `@inject`), `@nivinjoseph/n-log` (a `Logger` MUST be registered under the DI key `"Logger"`), `@nivinjoseph/n-defensive` (`given(...)` assertions — every n-eda runtime error is a `given(...)` message), `@nivinjoseph/n-exception` (`ApplicationException`, `ObjectDisposedException`, `ArgumentException`), `@nivinjoseph/n-ext` (prototype extensions incl. `getTypeName()`, loaded as a side effect), `ioredis` (you construct the client and register it as `"EdaRedisClient"`).

Reserved DI keys n-eda owns: `"EventBus"`, `"EventSubMgr"`, `"EdaContext"`, and every event handler class name.
DI keys YOU must provide: `"EdaRedisClient"` (an ioredis `Redis`), `"Logger"` (an n-log `Logger`).

## Exports

- `EdaManager` — the root object; wraps an n-ject `Container`, owns config and lifecycle (`bootstrap`, `beginConsumption`, `dispose`, `mapToPartition`)
- `EdaEvent` — event interface: `id`, `name`, `partitionKey`, `refId`, `refType`; extends n-util `Serializable`
- `EdaEventHandler<TEvent>` — handler INTERFACE (`implements`, never `extends`): `handle(event)`
- `event(EventClass)` — class decorator binding a handler to an event type
- `Topic` — `new Topic(name, ttlDuration, numPartitions)`; chain `.subscribe()`, `.forcePublish()`, `.flushConsume()`, `.configurePartitionAffinity("0-49")`, `.disable()`
- `EventBus` — publish interface: `publish(topic, ...events)`, `subscribeToObservables`, `unsubscribeFromObservables`; resolve via key `"EventBus"`
- `EventSubMgr` — subscription interface: `consume()` (never resolves until dispose)
- `RedisEventBus`, `RedisEventSubMgr` — the only shipped implementations; both `@inject("EdaRedisClient")`
- `EdaContext` — scoped, `get topic()`; inject as `"EdaContext"`. Throws under lambda/rpc/grpc consumers
- `EventRegistration` — reflected handler metadata; `static generateObservationKey(observer, observable, event)` → `.Observer.Observable.Event`
- `ObserverEdaEventHandler<TEvent>` — observer handler INTERFACE: `handle(event, observerId)` (note the 2nd arg)
- `observedEvent(EventClass)`, `observable(Type)`, `observer(Type)` — the three decorators an observer handler needs; ALL THREE required together
- `ObservableWatch` — `{ observableType, observableId, observableEventType }`; pass CLASS REFERENCES, not strings
- `discoverEventHandlers(directoryUrl: URL)` — convention-based discovery; returns `Promise<Array<EventHandlerClass>>`
- `LambdaDetails` — `{ region, funcName, credentials: { accessKeyId, accessKeySecret } }`
- `RpcDetails` — `{ host, port }`
- `GrpcDetails` — `{ host, port, isSecure?, connectionPoolSize? }` (`isSecure` is ignored)
- `AwsLambdaEventHandler`, `RpcEventHandler`, `GrpcEventHandler` — receive proxied events out of process
- `RpcServer`, `GrpcServer` — host the executing side; `new X(port, host|null, container, logger?)`, `.registerEventHandler(h)`, `.bootstrap()` (SYNC)
- `ApplicationScript` — `{ run(): Promise<void> }`; startup/shutdown hooks for the servers
- `NedaClearTrackedKeysEvent` — internal system event; fans out to all partitions and clears dedupe tracking

NOT exported (do not import): `InMemoryEventBus`, `InMemoryEventSubMgr` (commented out of the barrel), `Duration` (that is `@nivinjoseph/n-util`), `DefaultEdaContext`, `RpcModel`, `GrpcModel`, `TopicPartitionMetrics`.

## Minimal correct skeletons

Event:

```typescript
@serialize("MyApp")                                     // namespace REQUIRED on the class
export class UserCreatedEvent extends Serializable implements EdaEvent
{
    private readonly _id: string;
    private readonly _userId: string;

    @serialize                                          // REQUIRED
    public get id(): string { return this._id; }

    @serialize                                          // REQUIRED — routing depends on it
    public get name(): string { return (<Object>UserCreatedEvent).getTypeName(); }

    @serialize
    public get userId(): string { return this._userId; }

    public get partitionKey(): string { return this._userId; }   // NOT serialized — ordering key
    public get refId(): string { return this._userId; }          // NOT serialized — observer only
    public get refType(): string { return "User"; }              // NOT serialized — observer only

    public constructor(data: { id: string; userId: string; })
    {
        super(data);                                    // FIRST
        const { id, userId } = data;
        given(id, "id").ensureHasValue().ensureIsString();
        this._id = id;
        given(userId, "userId").ensureHasValue().ensureIsString();
        this._userId = userId;
    }
}
```

Handler:

```typescript
@event(UserCreatedEvent)                                // n-eda decorator ON TOP
@inject("Logger", "EventBus")                           // n-ject decorator BELOW it
export class UserCreatedEventHandler implements EdaEventHandler<UserCreatedEvent>
{                                                       // implements, NOT extends
    private readonly _logger: Logger;
    private readonly _eventBus: EventBus;

    public constructor(logger: Logger, eventBus: EventBus)
    {
        given(logger, "logger").ensureHasValue().ensureIsObject();
        this._logger = logger;
        given(eventBus, "eventBus").ensureHasValue().ensureIsObject();
        this._eventBus = eventBus;
    }

    public async handle(event: UserCreatedEvent): Promise<void>
    {
        await this._logger.logInfo(event.userId);
    }
}
```

Installer (without this, `bootstrap()` throws — `RedisEventBus` cannot resolve its client):

```typescript
export class CommonComponentInstaller implements ComponentInstaller
{
    public async install(registry: Registry): Promise<void>
    {
        const edaRedisClient = new Redis();
        const edaRedisClientDisposable = new DisposableWrapper(async () =>
        {
            await Delay.seconds(5);
            await new Promise<void>((resolve) =>
            {
                edaRedisClient.quit(() => resolve()).catch(e => console.error(e));
            });
        });

        registry
            .registerInstance("Logger", new ConsoleLogger())
            .registerInstance("EdaRedisClient", edaRedisClient)
            .registerInstance("EdaRedisClientDisposable", edaRedisClientDisposable);
    }
}
```

Wiring:

```typescript
const userTopic = new Topic("user", Duration.fromHours(1), 25).subscribe();   // .subscribe() REQUIRED to consume

const edaManager = new EdaManager();
edaManager
    .useInstaller(new CommonComponentInstaller())
    .useConsumerName("user-service")
    .registerTopics(userTopic)
    .registerEventHandlers(UserCreatedEventHandler)
    .registerEventBus(RedisEventBus)                                          // REQUIRED
    .registerEventSubscriptionManager(RedisEventSubMgr, "user-service-group");

await edaManager.bootstrap();                                                 // ASYNC — await it

edaManager.beginConsumption().catch(e => console.error(e));                   // NEVER await this

const eventBus = edaManager.serviceLocator.resolve<EventBus>("EventBus");
await eventBus.publish("user", new UserCreatedEvent({ id: "evt-1", userId: "usr-1" }));

await edaManager.dispose();
```

Handler discovery (replaces the hand-written list):

```typescript
edaManager.registerEventHandlers(
    ...await discoverEventHandlers(new URL("./event-handlers", import.meta.url)));
// convention: file `<name>-event-handler.js`, class `<Pascal>EventHandler`, has @event + handle()
// `import.meta.url` — NEVER a cwd-derived path; discovery scans EMITTED .js
```

Observer handler (all three decorators, `handle` takes a 2nd arg):

```typescript
@observedEvent(OrderShippedEvent)   // the event to watch
@observable(Order)                  // the type emitting it
@observer(Customer)                 // the type watching
export class CustomerOrderShippedHandler implements ObserverEdaEventHandler<OrderShippedEvent>
{
    public async handle(event: OrderShippedEvent, observerId: string): Promise<void> { }
}

// enable on BOTH sides:
edaManager.enableDistributedObserver(new Topic("observer", Duration.fromHours(1), 25).subscribe());

// subscribe (observer side) — the observable's event must set refType === "Order", refId === orderId
await eventBus.subscribeToObservables(Customer, customerId, [
    { observableType: Order, observableId: orderId, observableEventType: OrderShippedEvent }]);
```

## Rules the type system does not enforce

1. **`@serialize("Namespace")` on the event class, and bare `@serialize` on BOTH `id` and `name`.** `name` drives handler routing; without it the consumer cannot dispatch. Do NOT serialize `partitionKey`/`refId`/`refType` — they are derived on both sides. Omitting any of this compiles fine and fails at runtime.
2. **`name` must be `(<Object>MyEvent).getTypeName()`**, cast through `Object`. It is the routing key and the persisted identity — renaming an event class breaks deserialization of every in-flight event of that type.
3. **`EdaEventHandler` and `ObserverEdaEventHandler` are interfaces.** Use `implements`. `extends` does not compile.
4. **`@event(...)` goes ABOVE `@inject(...)`.**
5. **Handler class names are DI keys — globally unique.** Also: exactly one handler class per event type, and one per observation key. Violations throw at `registerEventHandlers`.
6. **Topics are publish-only by default.** `new Topic(...)` has `publishOnly === true`. Without `.subscribe()` the service publishes correctly and silently never consumes.
7. **`await bootstrap()`** — it is async (breaking change in 7.0.0).
8. **Never `await beginConsumption()`** — it is the consume loop and does not resolve until `dispose()`. Awaiting it hangs startup.
9. **Events with no locally-registered handler are silently DROPPED at publish time.** A dedicated publisher service (one that emits events it does not itself consume) writes nothing until you call `.forcePublish()` on the topic. This is the sharpest edge in the library.
10. **An installer registering `"EdaRedisClient"` and `"Logger"` is mandatory.** `bootstrap()` throws without it. n-eda never closes the Redis client — register a `Disposable` too.
11. **Topic TTL rounds to whole minutes.** `Duration.fromSeconds(20)` → 0 minutes → Redis `ERR invalid expire time`. Use >= 1 minute.
12. **`numPartitions` is effectively immutable.** Partition = `murmurhash3 x86 hash32(partitionKey) % numPartitions`; changing it rehashes every key, breaks per-key ordering, and orphans events in partitions nobody reads.
13. **Scaling a consumer group past one replica requires manual, disjoint `.configurePartitionAffinity("0-49")` ranges.** There is no rebalancing, no ownership lease, no heartbeat — replicas sharing a `consumerGroupId` share one read offset and will both dispatch the same events.
14. **`cleanUpKeys()` is destructive across consumer groups.** It deletes event payloads right after this group reads them. Safe only when exactly one group consumes the topic.
15. **No dead-letter queue.** A failing handler is retried 10 times over ~8.5 minutes (`(5+n)*n` seconds), then the event is dropped and marked processed. A poison event stalls its partition's batch window for that duration. Handlers must be idempotent — delivery is at-least-once with only a 1000-event dedupe window per (topic, partition, group).
16. **`usePartitionKeyMapper` may be called once.** Unset, it defaults to `event.partitionKey`.
17. **`Duration` is `@nivinjoseph/n-util`, not n-eda.** n-eda does not re-export it.
18. **The topic string in `publish(topic, ...)` must exactly match a registered `Topic.name`** — the lookup is case-sensitive even though duplicate detection is not.
19. **All configuration must precede `bootstrap()`.** Every `use*`/`register*`/`proxyTo*`/`actAs*` method throws `invoking method after bootstrap` afterwards.
20. **`EdaContext.topic` throws under the AWS Lambda, RPC, and gRPC consumers** — it is only populated on the in-process Redis consume path.
21. **`EdaManager.dispose()` disposes the container even when you supplied it.** If you passed your own `Container`, expect it to be disposed — and note that you, not n-eda, must have bootstrapped it.
22. **Run Redis with `maxmemory-policy noeviction`.** The write-index, read-index, and tracked-keys keys carry no TTL. Evicting the write index resets it to 0 while the read index stays high, which stops consumption permanently and silently.

## Reference implementation

- `test/utils/eda-test-utils.ts` — complete working setup: events, handlers, installer, configured `EdaManager`
- `test/eda.test.ts` — executable spec: publishes 10,000 events and asserts per-partition ordering against real Redis
- `README.md` — concepts, full API reference, best practices
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — Redis key layout, consume loop, delivery guarantees, tuning constants
- `docs/known-issues.md` — known defects and workarounds

When docs and code disagree, trust `test/`.
